findings.note: The noun 'realization' buries the verb 'realize', carried by the weak phrase 'come to'.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: Buried verb 'decide' is nominalized as 'decision', carried by the weak verb phrase 'was made'.
Buried verb 'evaluate' is nominalized as 'evaluation', carried by the phrasal verb 'carried out'.
The clause uses an impersonal passive construction without identifying who is doing the noting.
The draft does not state who forgot the combination, though it is likely the author.
The distinctive adjective 'picturesque' appears twice in consecutive sentences within this paragraph.

findings.quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences follow the same template: 'I [verb] ... at/by [time/place]'. The first occurrence is 'I left the house at six-forty.'
This stock phrase delays the statement without adding meaning.
Intensifier that adds emphasis without adding meaning.
"basically" is an empty hedge that adds no meaning to the statement of forgetting.

findings.quote: so this is my attempt at one.
findings.note: Throat-clearing. Announces the essay's purpose which is already evident from the title and preceding sentence.

findings.quote: which may or may not resemble yours.
findings.note: Stacked qualification. 'May or may not' is redundant hedging following 'own circumstances'.

findings.quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Run of three sentences opening with 'I [verb]'.

findings.quote: A monthly bus pass costs sixty.
findings.note: The previous sentence lists car expenses totaling six thousand. This sentence introduces the cost of a bus pass, linking only by implication of comparison rather than explicit transition.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city specify
findings.note: The previous sentence ends on the narrator's arrival at work. This sentence opens on municipal snow contracts, which were not mentioned earlier.
The previous sentence discusses crossing the bridge on foot, not the bike itself.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored to my own small concerns
findings.note: Mixed figure. The car is simultaneously described as a 'cocoon' (enclosure) and an 'anchor' (tether), images with conflicting spatial logic.

findings.quote: the city opened up like a book
findings.note: Stock image. A cliché comparison that does not specify what aspect of the city was revealed or how it functions as a text.
Doubled pair where 'complete' repeats the meaning of 'full'.
The subject-verb pair 'the board reviewed' is used twice within three sentences (second sentence: 'the board reviewed only', sixth sentence: 'the board reviewed eleven').
The word 'cumbersome' appears in the second sentence and again here.

findings.quote: The board meets on Thursday afternoons. The board makes a determination on each change during the meeting. The board then posts its decisions in the release channel.
findings.note: Run of three sentences opening with "The board".
The noun 'criticism' buries the verb 'criticize'. The main verb 'is' is weak.
The noun 'determination' buries the verb 'determine', carried by the weak verb 'makes'.
The verb 'conduct' is weak, carrying the action noun 'review'. The action is reviewing.
"quite" adds emphasis without changing the meaning of "encouraging".
Claims obviousness without adding meaning.
The draft does not state who raised these concerns.
The draft does not state who made the decision to require board sign-off for all changes.
The sentence opens with the passive 'It' referring to a decision, while the previous sentence focused on the wait time for a specific change.
The previous sentence was about leads recording approvals. This sentence opens on admission controllers, which are not mentioned until late in the clause.

findings.quote: Two months is a short period,
findings.note: The sentence opens with 'Two months', which refers to the duration of the pilot mentioned in a previous paragraph, not the immediate preceding sentence about the risk of misunderstanding.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Empty figure. The literal claim is that the board adds delay and friction; the image adds no specific mechanism beyond what 'cumbersome' already states.
Throat-clearing/commentary. The preceding sentence already presents the positive results (reduced wait, no rollbacks); this adds no new fact.

findings.quote: Concerns have been raised about the delays for over a year.
findings.note: Throat-clearing/Restatement. The draft has already argued the board is a 'toll booth' and the schedule 'made sense only when releases were rare.' Stating that concerns exist repeats the problem definition without adding new evidence.

findings.quote: I want to be clear that this proposal is not a criticism of the board or of the people on it, who have given a great deal of their time over the years.
findings.note: Throat-clearing/Apology. This sentence defends against a criticism not explicitly made elsewhere. The next sentence ('Nor is it an attempt to remove oversight...') covers the substantive concern about governance. The personal defense of the board's effort is extraneous to the operational proposal.
The sentence opens on Tom, who was not mentioned in the previous sentence about the smell of flour.

The sentence opens with 'Gluten development', a technical concept not present in the previous sentence about Tom driving to buy flour. There is no clear link between buying flour and gluten chemistry.
"really" adds emphasis but no meaning.
"obviously" claims self-evidence not established by the text.
The intensifier 'very' adds emphasis but no specific meaning to the size of the kitchen.

findings.quote: It was obviously a shock to the whole street.
findings.note: Throat-clearing: announces the emotional impact which is immediately described by the metaphor that follows.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.
findings.note: Throat-clearing: Announces the scope of the following sentences without adding information.

findings.quote: It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street, and it would be impossible to describe every way in which their lives were changed by it.
findings.note: Restatement: Repeats the point made in the preceding sentence ('affected... in many different ways') using hyperbolic qualifiers.
The verb 'made' is weak because it carries the noun 'decision'. The action is deciding.
The noun 'undertaking' hides the verb 'undertake'. The main verb 'has given' is weak.
The noun 'assessment' hides the verb 'assess'. The phrasal verb 'carry out' is weak.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The agency responsible for issuing the warnings is not named.
The entity that made the promise regarding sandbags is not identified.
Stock image used as a summary of impact without detailing what specifically woke up or changed beyond physical repairs.
Stock image. It describes pressure without detailing what action was demanded or taken.
The word 'sodden' appears twice in consecutive sentences.
Doubled pair 'each and every' in the first sentence.

findings.quote: Some lost stock and some lost income, and some lost things that are harder to put a price on.
findings.note: The template "some lost" is repeated three times within two sentences.
"way" appears in the first sentence ("different ways") and again here.
The phrase 'flood wall' appears twice within three sentences (first in sentence 4, second in sentence 5).

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: The template 'It is a feeling that...' is used in two consecutive sentences.
The root 'decid-' appears in 'decided' and 'decision' within the same sentence.

findings.quote: Unfortunately, the meeting was conducted in a manner that was really quite unproductive.
findings.note: Stacked qualification: 'really' and 'quite' are redundant intensifiers for 'unproductive'.
Stock phrase delaying the content of the chair's statement.
Claim of feeling that adds no factual content.
Intensifier that adds emphasis but no meaning.
Intensifier that adds emphasis but no meaning.

findings.quote: a resolution would be arrived at
findings.note: The draft does not state who was expected to arrive at the resolution.
The actor responsible for failing to reach a resolution is not named in this sentence.
The phrase uses the weak verb 'was' with the action noun 'expectation'. The verb 'expect' exists.
The phrase uses the weak verb 'made' with the action noun 'observation'. The verb 'observe' exists.

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that a decision would be made
findings.note: The noun 'decision' buries the verb 'decide'. The main verbs 'was decided' and 'would be made' are passive or empty, leaving no active agent for the determination.
Run of three sentences opening with 'It is a'. The third sentence repeats the construction.
